verdict_vs_market.quote: In other words, Google has offered you a respectable median package, not a premium package for a passive candidate

verdict_vs_current.quote: Google is only $104,000 ahead over four years, or about $26,000/year—a 5% premium.

recommendation.quote: I would negotiate aggressively rather than accept or walk away now.

equity_grounding.quote: That places your request toward the upper end of reported L6 compensation, but still within a plausible range: recent data puts reported L6 PM TC at roughly $514K median and $671K at the 90th percentile nationally

uses_public_incumbent_benchmark.quote: That is almost exactly the reported Bay Area median for a Google L6 Senior PM—roughly $551,000

refresh_valued_at.quote: Do not count unspecified refresh grants when deciding. Treat them as potential upside—not part of the offer.

level_claim.quote: You are already at the equivalent broad seniority level at Meta.

walkaway_tied_to.quote: Walk if they barely improve: Given that you are happy at Meta, I would probably stay if Google only adds something like a $25K–$50K sign-on

ask_focus.quote: “My preference is $265K base, $1.3M in equity and a $150K sign-on.

rsu_annualized.quote: RSUs: $270,000/year when simply divided across four years

year1_vs_recurring.quote: That equals $600K recurring annualized TC and $625K four-year average including the sign-on.

forfeiture_as_loss.quote: Preferably $100K+ sign-on to compensate for transition risk and forfeited vesting/timing.
